root_cause.text: The DMA channel deallocation in s3c64xx_spi_remove() was left in place after DMA channel allocation was moved from probe() to s3c64xx_spi_prepare_transfer(), causing a NULL-pointer dereference on driver unbind when the channels were never allocated.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "A change moving DMA channel allocation from probe() back to s3c64xx_spi_prepare_transfer() failed to remove the corresponding deallocation from remove(). Drop the bogus DMA channel release from remove() to avoid triggering a NULL-pointer dereference on driver unbind." The patch removes the `if (!is_polling(sdd)) { dma_release_channel(sdd->rx_dma.ch); dma_release_channel(sdd->tx_dma.ch); }` block from the remove function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove DMA channel release in spi remove to prevent double release or incorrect resource handling in the s3c64xx SPI driver.
intent_record.what: Removed the conditional release of DMA channels (rx and tx) inside the s3c64xx_spi_remove function, which was executed when the SPI controller was not in polling mode.
intent_record.how: During driver removal, DMA channels are no longer released via dma_release_channel(), potentially avoiding a double release if those channels are freed elsewhere, or correcting resource ownership.
